question: What is the primary objective of intra-natal care?

options.A: Ensuring the mother remains completely silent
options.B: Achieving a safe outcome for mother and baby
options.C: Preventing the need for any postpartum drugs
options.D: Speeding up the duration of the first stage

explanation: Intra-natal care focuses heavily on safeguarding both maternal and neonatal health during childbirth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h1)

question: Why should birth attendants maintain emergency readiness during every normal labour?

options.A: Emergency trays help keep the delivery suite looking organized
options.B: Normal labours can unexpectedly develop life-threatening complications
options.C: Hospital regulations require strict equipment display in all rooms
options.D: Complications only happen when midwives fail to monitor early

explanation: Childbirth is notoriously unpredictable, meaning a low-risk labour can suddenly require urgent intervention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h1)

question: When does the second stage of labour officially begin?

options.B: At the rupture of the membranes

explanation: The second stage starts when the cervix reaches ten centimeters of dilatation and ends with baby birth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h2)

question: What is the main clinical focus during the fourth stage of labour?

options.A: Encouraging the mother to walk around the ward
options.B: Repairing deep perineal tears under general anesthesia
options.C: Teaching the mother advanced infant feeding techniques
options.D: Monitoring for postpartum hemorrhage and uterine atony

explanation: The immediate two hours post-delivery carry the highest risk of primary postpartum hemorrhage, requiring vigilant observation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h2)

question: When is the best time to auscultate the fetal heart rate during labour?

options.C: Only when the mother pushes actively
options.D: While the uterine contraction is peaking

explanation: Listening right after a contraction allows the nurse to hear how the fetus recovers from the stress of uterine compression. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h3)

question: What does thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid indicate when membranes rupture?

options.B: Rapid dilatation of the uterine cervix

explanation: Passing meconium in utero often happens when the fetus experiences oxygen deprivation, causing sphincter relaxation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h3)

question: At what cervical dilatation does active partograph plotting typically begin?
explanation: The active phase of labour, where the partograph starts, is conventionally marked at four centimeters of cervical dilatation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h4)

question: What action is required when a laboring woman's cervical dilatation crosses the action line on the partograph?

options.A: Waiting another four hours to see if spontaneous progress occurs
options.B: Immediate clinical review and possible transfer for emergency care
options.C: Discharging the patient home for rest until contractions return
options.D: Stopping all forms of maternal hydration and pain management

explanation: Crossing the action line indicates abnormal progress that requires urgent medical management to prevent obstructed labour. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h4)

question: Which of the following practices helps prevent puerperal sepsis during vaginal examinations?

options.A: Strict adherence to hand hygiene and sterile gloves
options.C: Applying heavy powder to the examination table
options.D: Using cold water to rinse the perineal area

explanation: Proper hand hygiene and sterile barrier methods prevent the introduction of pathogenic bacteria into the reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h5)

question: Why should perineal cleansing be performed in a downward direction away from the vagina?

options.A: To stimulate effective uterine contractions in women with slow labour
options.B: To dry the perineal skin thoroughly before the baby is born
options.C: To prevent transferring fecal bacteria from the anus to the birth canal
options.D: To increase the speed of cervical dilatation during the first stage

explanation: Wiping downward avoids contaminating the vaginal opening with microorganisms from the perianal region. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of immediate newborn care in the delivery room?

options.A: Weighing the infant immediately before drying occurs
options.B: Establishing respiration and maintaining normal body temperature
options.D: Measuring head circumference and body length

explanation: A newborn must transition to extrauterine life by breathing effectively and avoiding dangerous hypothermia. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h6)

question: What intervention is required for a newborn who is limp and not breathing at birth?

options.A: Wrapping the baby tightly in cold wet towels for stimulation
options.B: Waiting five minutes to see if spontaneous breathing starts
options.C: Initiating positive pressure ventilation with a bag and mask
options.D: Administering oral glucose water immediately via a syringe

explanation: An unresponsive, non-breathing newborn requires immediate ventilation during the golden minute to prevent brain damage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h6)

question: What is the initial nursing action when an umbilical cord prolapses during labour?

options.A: Instructing the mother to bear down and push harder
options.B: Applying warm packs to the maternal lower abdomen
options.C: Manually elevating the presenting part off the cord
options.D: Pushing the visible cord loops back inside the uterus

explanation: Keeping the presenting part elevated relieves compression on the umbilical cord, preserving blood flow to the fetus. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h7)

question: Why is excessive traction on the fetal head dangerous during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: It accelerates cervical dilatation beyond safe limits
options.B: It triggers immediate maternal postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: It forces meconium into the lower respiratory tract
options.D: It can cause permanent brachial plexus nerve injury

explanation: Pulling hard on the head stretches the brachial plexus nerves, leading to arm weakness or paralysis in the baby. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h7)

question: When should clinical observations and interventions be documented during labour?

options.C: At the end of the shift before leaving

explanation: Recording events as they happen prevents memory lapses and ensures a legally reliable medical record. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h8)

question: Why is a standardized referral form essential when transferring a patient to a higher facility?

options.A: It clearly communicates clinical findings and urgency to the receiving team
options.B: It serves as a receipt for hospital financial accounting officers
options.C: It prevents the need for any verbal communication between nurses
options.D: It allows the patient to choose her preferred doctor on arrival

explanation: A structured referral summary ensures the receiving facility understands the background and exact care needed immediately. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h8)
